haiku-low.q1: Only the most recent missed fire time gets a run. Earlier missed fire times are silently dropped, with no history entry.
haiku-low.q2: The new fire time is recorded as a run with status skipped, with no attempts and finished_at set to now().
haiku-low.q3: Up to 3 attempts. Wait 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. After the third failure the run ends as failed.
haiku-low.q4: After its heartbeat is over 2 minutes old, the reaper marks it abandoned. Yes, that uses one of the 3 attempts.
haiku-low.q5: The executing job finishes normally. The queued unstarted job is cancelled. Fire times during the pause create no runs; after resume, missed fire times are never caught up.
haiku-low.q6: The schedule row lock via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, plus the UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) constraint. next_fire_at advances in the same transaction.
haiku-low.q7: In job_schedules.next_fire_at. It changes on fire, on re-enable, on resume, on cron or timezone edit, and is set to NULL on disable.
haiku-low.q8: It selects one queued run with next_attempt_at <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, then sets it running and increments attempts_used in one transaction.
haiku-low.q9: In job_runs.heartbeat_at. The worker updates it every 30 seconds. The reaper notices when it is older than 2 minutes.
haiku-low.q10: In job_runs.next_attempt_at: now()+1 minute after attempt 1, now()+5 minutes after attempt 2. The run is claimed once that time has passed.
haiku-low.q11: Once per fire time: a job_runs row. Once per execution try: a job_attempts row.
haiku-low.q12: The fence: its writes match zero rows because attempts_used no longer equals its attempt number and status is no longer running. It writes nothing and rolls back.

sonnet.q1: Only one run is created, for the most recent missed fire time; the earlier two are silently dropped with no history. If the schedule still has an in-progress run, that new run is recorded as skipped instead of queued. Stale running rows are reaped.
sonnet.q2: The new run is inserted with status skipped, finished_at = now(), and no attempts, because the schedule already has a queued or running run. The schedule's next_fire_at still advances.
sonnet.q3: At most 3 attempts. Wait is 1 minute after attempt 1 and 5 minutes after attempt 2. After the third failed attempt (attempts_used >= 3) the run ends with status failed and finished_at set.
sonnet.q4: Once its heartbeat_at is older than 2 minutes, any worker's reaper (picked up a few seconds later, on the next poll) closes the attempt as abandoned and applies the retry rule. Yes, it uses up one of the 3 attempts. The run is requeued with a 1 or 5 minute delay (or failed if attempts_used >= 3), so it is claimable only after that delay.
sonnet.q5: The executing (running) job is not cancelled and finishes normally. The waiting job is cancelled if it is unstarted (queued with attempts_used=0); a queued job waiting out a retry (attempts_used>0) is kept and keeps retrying, per the stated assumption to confirm. During the pause the fire step skips the tenant's schedules, so no runs are created. On resume, paused_at is cleared and next_fire_at is recomputed to the first fire time after now(); missed fire times are never caught up.
sonnet.q6: The fire step selects due schedules with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so the second worker skips the locked schedule. next_fire_at advances in the same transaction, and UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING backs it up.
sonnet.q7: In job_schedules.next_fire_at (NULL when disabled), always strictly in the future. It is set to the first fire time after now() by the fire step in the same transaction that creates a run. It is also recomputed on re-enable, tenant resume, and edit of cron or timezone, and set to NULL on disable.
sonnet.q8: It selects one queued run with next_attempt_at <= now() using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so other workers skip the locked row. In the same transaction it re-checks status='queued', sets status='running', increments attempts_used, sets heartbeat_at = now(), and inserts a job_attempts row.
sonnet.q9: In job_runs.heartbeat_at, which the worker updates every 30 seconds (while status='running'). The reaper step of any worker notices when heartbeat_at < now() - 2 minutes.
sonnet.q10: In job_runs.next_attempt_at (now() + 1 minute after attempt 1 or +5 minutes after attempt 2), with status set back to queued and heartbeat_at cleared. The retry starts when a worker's claim step selects the queued run once next_attempt_at <= now().
sonnet.q11: Once per fire time: a job_runs row (unique on schedule_id, fire_time). Once per execution try: a job_attempts row (unique on run_id, attempt_no).
sonnet.q12: The fence. The takeover's claim incremented job_runs.attempts_used, and the stale worker's finishing updates require attempts_used = its old attempt number and status='running' (and the attempt row outcome='running', which the reaper had set to abandoned). They match zero rows, so the worker writes nothing and rolls back.
